tool_schemas.name: Optional Settings
tool_schemas.description: Manages stored Jira server connections and the credentials used to authenticate to them: you can list/get/create/update/delete servers, start/get/cancel/complete authentication sessions, list/get/revoke credentials, and verify a server connection; list actions return up to `limit` items (default server-side) ordered by `sort` and include an opaque `cursor` for fetching the next page. It validates ULID formats and required identifiers for each action (e.g., `jira_server_id` for get/update/delete/verify, `jira_auth_session_id` for get/cancel/complete, `jira_credential_id` for get/revoke), enforces `auth_type` and body shape for the chosen workflow (OAuth requires `redirect_uri`/`code` on completion; token flows require the corresponding token fields), and rejects invalid `limit`, `sort`, or body fields. Raises NOT_FOUND when the referenced workspace/user/server/session/credential does not exist or is not accessible to the caller; raises CONFLICT when an operation is not allowed for the current state (e.g., completing or canceling an auth session that is already completed/canceled/expired, verifying or updating a deleted server, revoking an already-revoked credential), and raises UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN when the caller lacks permission to manage the specified workspace/user resources.

action.description: Operation to perform for managing Jira server connections and authentication.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ULID (wrk_...) that owns the Jira server connection(s).

user_id.description: User ULID (usr_...) performing the action / owning credentials (when applicable).

jira_server_id.description: Jira server ULID (jrs_...) identifying a specific stored Jira connection.

jira_auth_session_id.description: Jira auth session ULID (jas_...) identifying a specific authentication flow session.

jira_credential_id.description: Jira credential ULID (jrc_...) identifying a stored credential/token record.

auth_type.description: Authentication method to use for a Jira server/session/credential.

status.description: Status filter or target status depending on action (varies by entity).

q.description: Free-text search query (typically matches Jira server name/base_url).

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return for list actions.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for list actions.

jira_server.description: Body for creating/updating a Jira server connection.

name.description: Display name for the Jira server connection.

base_url.description: Base URL of the Jira instance (e.g., https://your-domain.atlassian.net).

deployment_type.description: Jira deployment type for the target instance.

auth_type.description: Default authentication type to associate with this server connection.

status.description: Server connection status (typically managed by the system; may be set in admin workflows).

auth_session.description: Body for starting or completing an authentication session.

redirect_uri.description: Redirect URI to return to after Jira authorization (OAuth flows).

state_token.description: Client-provided state token for CSRF protection / correlating callbacks.

code.description: OAuth authorization code returned by Jira (for completing OAuth callback).

error_code.description: OAuth error code returned by Jira (if callback indicates an error).

error_message.description: OAuth error message returned by Jira (if callback indicates an error).

credential.description: Body for credential actions where direct token input may be required (non-OAuth flows).

username.description: Username/email for basic auth with API token (api_token_basic).

api_token.description: API token value for basic auth (api_token_basic); stored encrypted server-side.

personal_access_token.description: Personal access token value (personal_access_token); stored encrypted server-side.

scopes.description: Requested/associated scopes for the credential (primarily OAuth).
